metadata.description: Edni AI Question Bank — 3D tagged: Concept × Bloom Cognitive Dimension × Knowledge Dimension + 3PL IRT parameters

questions.question_text: What is the index of the first element in an array in most programming languages?
questions.explanation: Most languages use 0-based indexing.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the time complexity of accessing an element by index in an array?

options.B: O(log n)

questions.explanation: Arrays provide O(1) access via direct memory addressing.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: When a dynamic array doubles capacity, what is the amortized time complexity of append?

options.B: O(log n)

questions.explanation: Amortized analysis shows append is O(1) even with occasional O(n) resizing.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: In row-major order, which elements are stored contiguously in memory?

options.B: Diagonal elements

questions.explanation: Row-major stores all elements of a row contiguously.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Which scenario best justifies choosing an array over a linked list?

options.B: Unknown data size at compile time

questions.explanation: Arrays excel at O(1) random access.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What does a node in a singly linked list contain?

options.B: Data and a pointer to next node

questions.explanation: A singly linked list node contains data and one next pointer.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the time complexity of inserting a node at the beginning of a singly linked list?

options.B: O(log n)

questions.explanation: Inserting at head only requires updating the head pointer.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: How do you detect the end of a singly linked list during traversal?

options.B: When next pointer is NULL

questions.explanation: The last node's next pointer is NULL.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Floyd's cycle detection uses two pointers. What are their speeds?

options.B: Slow moves 1, fast moves 2

questions.explanation: Floyd's: slow pointer 1 step, fast pointer 2 steps.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the main trade-off of a doubly linked list over singly linked list?

options.B: Extra memory for backward pointer

questions.explanation: Doubly linked lists store an extra prev pointer, increasing memory.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What does LIFO stand for?

options.B: Last In Fast Out

questions.explanation: LIFO: the last element inserted is the first removed.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Which operation removes and returns the top element from a stack?

options.B: Peek

questions.explanation: Pop removes and returns the top element.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Which is a classic application of a stack?

options.B: Function call management

questions.explanation: The call stack manages function calls and return addresses.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: To check balanced parentheses using a stack, what do you do when you encounter a closing bracket?

options.B: Pop and check if it matches

questions.explanation: Pop and verify it matches the corresponding opening bracket.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What causes a stack overflow in recursive programs?

options.B: Infinite or too-deep recursion exceeding stack memory

questions.explanation: Deep recursion keeps adding frames until memory is exhausted.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What principle does a queue follow?

options.B: FIFO

questions.explanation: FIFO: First In First Out.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Which operation adds an element to the rear of a queue?

options.B: Push

questions.explanation: Enqueue adds an element to the rear.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Why is a circular queue preferred over linear for fixed-size buffers?

options.B: Avoids false overflow by reusing freed front slots

questions.explanation: Circular queues wrap around, reusing dequeued slots.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What data structure is typically used to implement an efficient priority queue?

options.B: Linked List

questions.explanation: A binary heap provides O(log n) insert and extract operations.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Which traversal algorithm uses a queue as its primary data structure?

options.B: Inorder

questions.explanation: BFS uses a queue to explore nodes level by level.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the maximum number of children a node can have in a binary tree?
questions.explanation: A binary tree node has at most 2 children: left and right.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: In a BST, where are values smaller than the root stored?

options.B: Left subtree

questions.explanation: BST: left subtree has values less than root.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the height of a complete binary tree with n nodes?

options.B: O(n²)

questions.explanation: Each level doubles nodes, giving O(log n) height.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the balance factor condition for an AVL tree node?

options.B: Between -2 and 2

questions.explanation: AVL trees maintain balance factor of -1, 0, or 1.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: In which traversal order do you visit: Left, Root, Right?

options.B: Postorder

questions.explanation: Inorder: Left, Root, Right — produces sorted output for BSTs.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is a directed graph also called?

options.B: Digraph

questions.explanation: A directed graph is called a digraph.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: For a sparse graph, which representation is more memory-efficient?

options.B: Adjacency list

questions.explanation: Adjacency list uses O(V+E) vs O(V²) for matrix.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What data structure does Dijkstra's algorithm use to get the minimum distance node efficiently?

options.B: Queue

questions.explanation: A min-heap allows O(log V) extraction of minimum distance node.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Which algorithm guarantees shortest path in an unweighted graph?

options.B: BFS

questions.explanation: BFS guarantees shortest path in unweighted graphs by exploring level by level.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Topological sorting is only applicable to which type of graph?

options.B: Weighted graphs

questions.explanation: Cycles make topological ordering impossible; only DAGs qualify.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the worst-case time complexity of bubble sort?

options.B: O(n log n)

questions.explanation: Bubble sort has O(n²) worst case due to nested loops.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Merge sort is based on which algorithm design paradigm?

options.B: Dynamic Programming

questions.explanation: Merge sort divides, recursively sorts, then merges.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: When does Quick Sort degrade to O(n²)?

options.B: When pivot is always smallest or largest

questions.explanation: Consistently bad pivot creates unbalanced partitions leading to O(n²).
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Which sorting algorithm is stable?

options.B: Heap Sort

questions.explanation: Merge sort preserves relative order of equal elements.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: When is counting sort more efficient than comparison-based sorts?

options.B: When data range k is much smaller than n

questions.explanation: Counting sort is O(n+k); beats O(n log n) when k is small.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search?

options.B: O(log n)

questions.explanation: Linear search checks each element sequentially, giving O(n) worst case.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the prerequisite for binary search?

options.B: Data must be sorted

questions.explanation: Binary search requires sorted data to eliminate half the search space each step.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the average-case time complexity of search in a hash table?

options.B: O(log n)

questions.explanation: Hash tables provide O(1) average-case search.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Which collision resolution uses linked lists at each hash table slot?

options.B: Linear probing

questions.explanation: Separate chaining stores colliding elements in a linked list at the same slot.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: When does interpolation search outperform binary search?

options.B: When data is uniformly distributed

questions.explanation: Interpolation search achieves O(log log n) for uniformly distributed data.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is memoization in dynamic programming?

options.B: Storing results of subproblems to avoid recomputation

questions.explanation: Memoization caches subproblem results so they are computed only once.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Which property MUST a problem have for DP to apply?

options.B: Overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure

questions.explanation: DP requires overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Using DP, what is the time complexity of computing the nth Fibonacci number?

options.B: O(n²)

questions.explanation: DP reduces Fibonacci from O(2^n) to O(n).
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the time complexity of the 0/1 Knapsack DP solution?

options.B: O(n log n)

questions.explanation: DP table has n×W cells, each O(1), giving O(nW) total.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: When stack overflow is a concern with DP, which approach do you choose?

options.B: Bottom-up tabulation

questions.explanation: Bottom-up avoids recursion entirely, eliminating stack overflow risk.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What does O(1) time complexity mean?

options.B: Constant time

questions.explanation: O(1) means constant time regardless of input size.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the space complexity of an in-place sorting algorithm?

options.B: O(log n)

questions.explanation: In-place algorithms use O(1) extra space.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: Why might an O(n²) worst-case algorithm still be preferred in practice?

options.B: Average case is O(n log n) with small constants

questions.explanation: If average case and constants are better, practical performance may be superior.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What distinguishes an NP problem from a P problem?

options.B: NP can be verified in polynomial time but not necessarily solved

questions.explanation: NP: verifiable in polynomial time; whether solvable in polynomial time is the P=NP question.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: How would you decide between two algorithms with the same Big-O for a given problem?

options.B: Consider constants, memory, and input distribution

questions.explanation: When Big-O is equal, practical performance depends on constants, cache, and real-world input.
questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms

questions.question_text: What is the primary goal of software testing?

options.B: Find defects and assess quality

questions.explanation: Testing aims to find defects and assess quality, not prove correctness.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Which best describes validation?

options.A: Are we building the product right?
options.B: Are we building the right product?

questions.explanation: Validation: right product (user needs). Verification: built correctly.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Which testing level tests individual functions in isolation?

options.B: Integration testing

questions.explanation: Unit testing tests individual components in isolation.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: When is regression testing most important?

options.B: After code changes to ensure existing functionality still works

questions.explanation: Regression testing re-runs tests after changes to detect side effects.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: According to the test pyramid, which type of test should be most numerous?

options.B: Integration tests

questions.explanation: The pyramid advocates many fast unit tests at the base.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What is the AAA pattern in unit testing?

options.B: Arrange, Act, Assert

questions.explanation: AAA: Arrange (setup), Act (execute), Assert (verify).
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Why are mock objects used in unit testing?

options.B: To isolate the unit under test from dependencies

questions.explanation: Mocks simulate dependencies so the unit is tested in isolation.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What does 100% code coverage guarantee?

options.B: Every statement was executed during testing

questions.explanation: 100% coverage means every line executed, not all edge cases correct.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: In TDD, what is the correct order of steps?

options.B: Write test → Write code → Refactor

questions.explanation: TDD: Red (write failing test) → Green (pass) → Refactor.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of an assertion in a unit test?

options.B: Verify expected and actual values match

questions.explanation: Assertions verify actual matches expected, failing the test if not.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What is a disadvantage of big bang integration testing?

options.B: Difficult to isolate defects when all components integrated at once

questions.explanation: Big bang makes defect isolation hard since all components combined simultaneously.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: In top-down integration testing, what simulates lower-level modules not yet developed?

options.B: Stubs

questions.explanation: Stubs simulate lower-level modules in top-down testing.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Which HTTP status code indicates successful resource creation?

options.B: 201 Created

questions.explanation: 201 Created is the standard response for successful POST creating a resource.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What does consumer-driven contract testing primarily ensure?

options.B: The provider's API meets the consumer's expectations

questions.explanation: Consumer-driven contracts prevent provider breaking changes.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Why does CI help with integration testing?

options.B: Detects integration issues early by merging and testing frequently

questions.explanation: CI runs integration tests on every commit, catching issues early.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: In equivalence partitioning, why can one test case represent a whole partition?

options.B: All values in a partition behave the same way

questions.explanation: All values in a class produce the same system behavior.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: For a field accepting 1-100, which values would BVA test?
questions.explanation: BVA: boundaries and just outside: 0,1,2,99,100,101.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Decision table testing is most effective when?

options.B: Multiple conditions combine to produce different actions

questions.explanation: Decision tables excel when multiple conditions determine different behaviors.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: State transition testing is best applied to systems that:

options.B: Change behavior based on history of inputs/states

questions.explanation: State transition testing models systems where behavior depends on current state.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What makes exploratory testing valuable beyond scripted testing?

options.B: Testers use intuition and creativity to find defects scripts miss

questions.explanation: Exploratory testing leverages expertise to discover unexpected defects.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What does statement coverage measure?

options.B: Percentage of statements executed by tests

questions.explanation: Statement coverage: percentage of code statements executed during testing.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Why is branch coverage stronger than statement coverage?

options.B: Ensures both true and false outcomes of conditions are tested

questions.explanation: Branch coverage ensures every decision outcome is tested.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Why is 100% path coverage often impractical?

options.B: Number of paths can be exponential due to loops

questions.explanation: Loops create exponentially many paths.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of mutation testing?

options.B: Assess how well tests detect intentionally introduced faults

questions.explanation: Mutation testing evaluates test suite strength by introducing small code faults.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Cyclomatic complexity of a function with 5 decision points is:
questions.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity = decision points + 1 = 5+1 = 6.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Which is typically included in a software test plan?

options.B: Scope, objectives, resources, schedule, and risk

questions.explanation: Test plan documents scope, objectives, resources, schedule, and risks.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: In risk-based testing, how are test priorities determined?

options.B: Based on likelihood and impact of failures

questions.explanation: Risk-based: prioritize areas with higher probability and greater business impact.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What is the correct order in a typical defect lifecycle?

options.B: Assign → Fix → Open → Close

questions.explanation: Standard defect flow: Open → Assign → Fix → Verify → Close.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: A cosmetic bug on the company logo has low severity but high priority. Why?

options.B: Brand visibility makes it urgent despite minimal technical impact

questions.explanation: Priority reflects business urgency independent of technical severity.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What does load testing measure?

options.B: System behavior under expected user load

questions.explanation: Load testing evaluates performance under anticipated concurrent user load.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: How does stress testing differ from load testing?

options.B: Stress pushes beyond normal limits to find breaking point

questions.explanation: Stress testing exceeds capacity to find where and how systems fail.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Which factor most determines if a test is a good automation candidate?

options.B: Frequency of execution and stability of functionality

questions.explanation: Frequently run, stable tests have the highest automation ROI.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: What is the main benefit of the Page Object Model in UI automation?

options.B: Separates UI structure from test logic improving maintainability

questions.explanation: POM encapsulates UI elements so UI changes only require updates in one place.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: When building a regression suite, how do you select which tests to include?

options.B: Prioritize high-risk areas, frequent failures, and core functionality

questions.explanation: Effective regression suites balance coverage and execution time by prioritizing risk and business-critical paths.
questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.question_text: Which phase of SDLC involves gathering user requirements?

options.B: Implementation

questions.explanation: Requirements phase: eliciting and documenting user needs.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What is a major disadvantage of the Waterfall model?

options.B: Difficult to accommodate changes after a phase is complete

questions.explanation: Waterfall is sequential; going back is costly.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What distinguishes the Spiral model from other SDLC models?

options.B: Emphasis on risk analysis in each iteration

questions.explanation: Spiral incorporates risk analysis at each iteration.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: When is prototyping most beneficial?

options.B: Requirements are unclear and user feedback needed early

questions.explanation: Prototyping clarifies vague requirements by giving users a tangible model.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: In the V-Model, acceptance testing corresponds to which phase?

options.B: Unit design

questions.explanation: V-Model pairs: requirements ↔ acceptance testing.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: Which is a functional requirement?

options.B: User can log in with email and password

questions.explanation: Functional requirements describe specific system behaviors.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: Performance, security, and scalability are examples of:

options.B: Non-functional requirements

questions.explanation: Non-functional requirements describe system quality attributes.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: In a use case, what is an 'actor'?

options.B: A person or system interacting with the system

questions.explanation: An actor is any entity that interacts with the system being developed.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What is the standard format for a user story?

options.B: As a [user], I want [goal] so that [reason]

questions.explanation: Standard user story captures role, goal, and business value.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: Why is requirements traceability important?

options.B: Links requirements to design, code, and tests ensuring all are implemented

questions.explanation: Traceability ensures every requirement is designed, coded, and tested.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What does high cohesion in a module indicate?

options.B: Elements are closely related and focused on one responsibility

questions.explanation: High cohesion: single, well-defined purpose — a positive design quality.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: Why is low coupling desirable?

options.B: Modules can be changed independently with minimal impact on others

questions.explanation: Low coupling enables independent development, testing, and modification.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What does the Singleton pattern ensure?

options.B: Only one instance of a class exists application-wide

questions.explanation: Singleton: exactly one instance with a global access point.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: The Observer pattern is best used when:

options.A: One object change should notify multiple dependent objects
options.B: Creating complex objects step by step
options.C: Providing simplified interface to a complex system

questions.explanation: Observer implements publish-subscribe: subject changes notify all observers.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What problem does the Factory Method pattern solve?

options.B: Decoupling object creation from the code that uses objects

questions.explanation: Factory Method decouples creation logic from usage.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: Who prioritizes the product backlog in Scrum?

options.B: Development Team

questions.explanation: The Product Owner owns and prioritizes the product backlog.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What is a Sprint in Scrum?

options.B: A fixed-length iteration delivering a potentially shippable increment

questions.explanation: Sprint: time-boxed iteration producing a usable product increment.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What is the main mechanism Kanban uses to control work in progress?

options.B: WIP limits on columns

questions.explanation: Kanban uses WIP limits to prevent overloading teams and maintain flow.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: In a UML class diagram, what does a filled diamond represent?

options.B: Aggregation

questions.explanation: Filled diamond = Composition: child cannot exist without parent.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What does a sequence diagram primarily show?

options.B: Time-ordered message interactions between objects

questions.explanation: Sequence diagrams show message passing in chronological order.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: The project management triangle consists of which three constraints?

options.B: Scope, Schedule, Cost

questions.explanation: Iron triangle: Scope, Schedule, Cost — changing one affects others.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What is the primary use of a Gantt chart?

options.B: Visualizing task schedule, duration, and dependencies over time

questions.explanation: Gantt charts provide a visual timeline of tasks, durations, and dependencies.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: In MVC, what is the role of the Controller?

options.B: Handles user input and updates Model and View

questions.explanation: Controller processes user input, updates Model, and selects View.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What is a key trade-off of microservices vs monolithic architecture?

options.B: Increased network complexity and operational overhead

questions.explanation: Microservices enable independent scaling but introduce distributed system complexity.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: Which maintenance type fixes bugs found after deployment?

options.B: Perfective

questions.explanation: Corrective maintenance addresses defects discovered post-deployment.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What is technical debt?

options.B: Cost of rework from shortcuts taken to deliver faster

questions.explanation: Technical debt: implied cost of future rework from quick solutions.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: Which technique is commonly used to identify project risks?

options.B: Brainstorming and risk checklists

questions.explanation: Brainstorming and checklists systematically uncover potential threats.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: In a risk matrix, how is risk level calculated?

options.B: Risk = Probability × Impact

questions.explanation: Risk = Probability × Impact, used to prioritize mitigation.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: Service-Oriented Architecture promotes:

options.B: Reusable, interoperable services over standard protocols

questions.explanation: SOA: interoperable services reusable across applications.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of event-driven architecture?

options.B: Loose coupling and high scalability through async event processing

questions.explanation: Event-driven: decouples producers from consumers enabling scalability.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: UML Activity diagrams are best used to model:

options.B: Workflow and process flow with decision points

questions.explanation: Activity diagrams model workflows with decision and parallel paths.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: How does DevOps differ from traditional approaches?

options.B: Integrates development and operations with CI/CD and automation

questions.explanation: DevOps bridges development and operations through CI/CD and shared responsibility.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: The Single Responsibility Principle states a class should:

options.B: Have only one reason to change

questions.explanation: SRP: one responsibility = one reason to change.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a Sprint Retrospective?

options.B: Review features with stakeholders
options.C: Reflect on team process and identify improvements

questions.explanation: Retrospective: what went well, what didn't, how to improve.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: For a new feature with high uncertainty, which estimation technique is most appropriate?

options.B: Three-point estimation (optimistic, most likely, pessimistic)

questions.explanation: Three-point estimation accounts for uncertainty by considering best, expected, and worst case.
questions.subject: Software Engineering

questions.question_text: Which is a primitive data type in Java?

options.B: ArrayList

questions.explanation: int is primitive in Java; others are reference types.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: In statically typed languages, when are type checks performed?

options.B: At compile time

questions.explanation: Static typing checks types at compile time.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: What is implicit type conversion (coercion)?

options.B: Automatic type conversion by the language

questions.explanation: Implicit coercion is automatic conversion without explicit programmer instruction.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: What is the scope of a variable declared inside a function?

options.B: File scope

questions.explanation: Variables declared inside a function are local to that function.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: In JavaScript, what is the key difference between const and let?

options.B: const cannot be reassigned after initialization

questions.explanation: const prevents reassignment; let allows it.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: Which loop guarantees execution of its body at least once?

options.B: while loop

questions.explanation: do-while executes body first, then checks condition.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: What happens in a switch without break in a case?

options.B: Fall-through: execution continues to next case

questions.explanation: Without break, execution falls through to the next case.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: In 'A && B', if A is false, what happens to B?

options.B: B is not evaluated (short-circuit)

questions.explanation: Short-circuit: in &&, if first is false, second is not evaluated.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: What are the two essential components of a recursive function?

options.B: Base case and recursive case

questions.explanation: Recursion needs base case (stop) and recursive case (self-call).
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: In try-catch-finally, when does the finally block execute?

options.B: Only when exception occurs

questions.explanation: finally always executes after try and catch.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: What does it mean for functions to be 'first-class citizens'?

options.B: Functions can be assigned, passed as arguments, and returned

questions.explanation: First-class: functions treated like any value — assigned, passed, returned.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: What is a closure?

options.A: A way to close a program
options.B: A function that retains access to variables from its enclosing scope
options.D: A method to end a loop

questions.explanation: Closure: function bundled with references to its surrounding lexical scope.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: What is the main difference between compiled and interpreted languages?

options.B: Compiled translates to machine code before run; interpreted translates at runtime

questions.explanation: Compiled: translate before execution. Interpreted: translate line-by-line at runtime.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: How would you decide between OOP and functional programming for a new module?

options.B: OOP for stateful systems with entities; FP for data transformation pipelines

questions.explanation: OOP suits state/entities; FP suits data transformation and immutability needs.
questions.subject: Programming Languages

questions.question_text: In a relational database, data is organized into:

options.B: Tables (relations)

options.B: Must be unique and not NULL

options.B: Referential integrity between two tables

questions.subject: Database Systems

options.B: Any minimal set of attributes that uniquely identifies a row

questions.explanation: Candidate key: any minimal attribute set that could serve as primary key.

questions.explanation: Referential integrity prevents orphan records — invalid FK raises constraint violation.

questions.subject: Database Systems

options.B: LEFT JOIN

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: Which SQL function counts the number of rows in a result set?

options.B: AVG()

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: First Normal Form (1NF) requires that:

options.B: Partial dependencies on a composite primary key

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: Third Normal Form (3NF) eliminates:

options.B: Transitive dependencies (non-key depends on another non-key)

questions.explanation: 3NF: 2NF plus no non-key attribute transitively depends on primary key.
questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: When might denormalization be preferred?

options.B: When read performance is critical and redundancy is acceptable

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: What does the 'A' in ACID stand for?

questions.explanation: ACID: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.
questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: Which isolation level prevents dirty reads but allows non-repeatable reads?

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: What does a ROLLBACK statement do?

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: What does COMMIT do?

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a database index?

options.B: Speed up data retrieval without scanning the entire table

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: Why is B-Tree the most common index structure?

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.explanation: EXPLAIN shows the optimizer's execution plan — useful for finding bottlenecks.
questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: What is the N+1 query problem?

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: Which NoSQL type stores data as flexible JSON-like documents?

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: When would you choose NoSQL over relational?

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: What is a key advantage of stored procedures?

Software Quality Assurance
questions.question_text: What is the role of automated tests in a CI/CD pipeline?

options.B: Provide fast feedback by running automatically on every code commit

questions.explanation: Automated tests in CI/CD give immediate feedback on every commit, catching regressions early.

questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance
questions.question_text: What is smoke testing?

options.B: A quick sanity check to verify basic functionality before deeper testing

questions.explanation: Smoke testing verifies the most critical functions work before investing in full testing.

questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance
questions.question_text: How does sanity testing differ from smoke testing?

options.B: Sanity focuses on a specific bug fix or feature after a minor change
options.C: Smoke is done by developers only

questions.explanation: Sanity: narrow check on a specific area after a small change. Smoke: broad check of critical paths.

questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance
questions.question_text: Control flow testing focuses on:

questions.explanation: Control flow testing verifies correct execution paths through conditional and loop structures.

questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance
questions.question_text: What does spike testing evaluate?

questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance
questions.question_text: Why are test exit criteria important in a test plan?

options.B: To define when testing is considered complete and release is approved

questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance
questions.question_text: What is the purpose of root cause analysis after a defect is found?

questions.explanation: RCA identifies why a defect occurred so the process can be improved to prevent recurrence.

questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance
questions.question_text: What is the key difference between alpha and beta testing?

questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance

questions.subject: Software Quality Assurance
questions.question_text: Data flow testing focuses on:

questions.question_text: In pass-by-value, modifying a parameter inside a function:

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question_text: A functional dependency A → B means:

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.subject: Database Systems
questions.question_text: When designing a database for sensitive user data (PII), what security measures would you implement?

options.A: Store all data in plaintext for speed
options.B: Encrypt sensitive fields, use least privilege roles, audit logs, and parameterized queries
options.D: Store data in files instead of DB

questions.explanation: Defense in depth: encryption at rest/transit, least privilege, audit trails, and SQL injection prevention.
